body.statement: The band-robust theorem already gives contact-stable whole-set coverage and conservative simultaneous leaf projections. The remaining question is whether, uniformly over the externally certified subclass and through changing zero-capacity contacts and optimal faces, one can derive an explicit score-to-statistic expansion for gridded support values, baseline-law constraints, and optimized leaf endpoints, prove a controlled uniform remainder and conditional multiplier approximation, and calibrate one common multiplier critical value over the finite direction-net-by-leaf index set. The target is the sharper local-mass leaf-endpoint excess \(O_P(r_n/p_{\min,n}+\mathsf R\delta_n+\sqrt{(V_c\log n+\log|\mathcal D_n|+\log(1/\alpha))/(np_{\min,n})})\), with arbitrary post-selection validity inherited from the simultaneous event. No whole-set coverage claim remains open.
body.justification: The direct stability theorem closes changing-contact whole-set coverage. What remains is the efficient score expansion, conditional multiplier coupling, and local-mass leaf calibration, none of which follows from envelope, moment, and entropy bounds alone.
body.gap: Existing directional-delta and support-boundary methods do not supply the score-to-statistic expansion for this nuisance-dependent obstacle and its optimized leaf projections. The robust theorem bypasses that gap for whole-set coverage, but not for the sharper local-mass multiplier rate.
body.consumer: Solving the residual question would sharpen the conservative simultaneous genomic-leaf intervals to the desired local-mass rate while preserving post-selection validity.

obligation.what_is_open: The missing step is a band-subclass-uniform asymptotic linearization that links the declared score class to the gridded support values, baseline-law constraints, and optimized leaf endpoints through changing optimal faces, followed by conditional validity of the one-common-multiplier critical value for that linked process.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen score assumptions impose only centering, an envelope moment bound, and an entropy bound. They define neither the statistics represented by the scores nor a uniform remainder or multiplier coupling. The admissible zero-score class satisfies every stated score condition but has multiplier critical value zero and cannot control a nondegenerate eligible-leaf mass error; thus the desired multiplier/leaf conclusion is not derivable from the declared primitives.
obligation.attempted: I derived a contact-set-uniform contraction of each obstacle by positive-part shifting and used it with the external nuisance band and the grid theorem. This closes the robust whole-set geometry without differentiating active faces. I then attempted to calibrate the baseline-law and leaf projections from the stated score process, but there is no declared score-to-statistic equation to which the moment and entropy controls can be applied; the zero-score witness confirms that this is not recoverable by empirical-process algebra alone.
obligation.partial_result:
The changing-contact geometry itself admits the following uniform bound.
For two nonnegative capacities \(u,u'\), set
\(\rho=\|u-u'\|_\infty\).  If \(f\in\mathcal S(u)\), define
\(C_\rho f=(f-\rho)_+\).  The positive-part map is nondecreasing and
one-Lipschitz, so \(C_\rho f\) remains nonnegative, nondecreasing, and
\(L\)-Lipschitz.  Since \(f\le u\le u'+\rho\), one also has
\(C_\rho f\le u'\), and
\(\|f-C_\rho f\|_\infty\le\rho\).  Interchanging \(u,u'\) proves
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal S(u),\mathcal S(u')\}\le\|u-u'\|_\infty,
\]
with no condition on either zero-capacity contact set.  Consequently, if
\(\rho_b=\max_{a,z}\|b_{a,z}-b'_{a,z}\|_\infty\) and
\(\rho_u=\max_{a,z}\|u_{a,z}-u'_{a,z}\|_\infty\), applying
\(C_{\rho_u}\) separately in the two arms gives
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal T(b,u),\mathcal T(b',u')\}
 \le2\rho_b+2\rho_u.
\]
On the event in the external-band prerequisite, every admissible nuisance
element in the band is within \(2r_n\) of the true nuisance.  Hence the
closure of the union of its admissible obstacle images is within
\(8r_n\) of the true curve set.  Expanding each gridded image by
\(2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), as justified by the grid theorem, gives an observable
robust-band whole-set superset that contains the true curve set on that event
and whose directed excess is at most
\(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), before any optional direction-net remainder.
Thus changing and even newly appearing contact sets do not obstruct the
whole-set rate.

What remains unproved is the simultaneous multiplier and leaf projection
part.  The current premises bound only the envelope, moment, and covering
numbers of \(\Psi_n\); no declared equation connects an element of
\(\Psi_n\) to the estimation error of a support value, a leaf numerator, a
leaf mass, or an endpoint optimizer, and no premise asserts a uniform
linearization remainder or conditional multiplier coupling.  This is a
logical, not merely technical, omission.  For example, take the score class
to consist of the zero function for every index in
\(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).  It is centered, has zero envelope
moment, and has covering number one, so all three stated score conditions
hold.  Nevertheless, for an eligible leaf \(G\) with \(P_X(G)=1/2\) and an
odd sample size \(n\), the empirical leaf mass cannot equal \(1/2\), whereas
the multiplier supremum of the zero score class and its critical value are
identically zero.  Hence the declared score conditions alone do not control
even the leaf-mass error, much less the optimized leaf endpoints.  A complete
positive theorem must first define the support and leaf statistics and prove
a band-subclass-uniform score expansion for them, including the optimizer's
changing critical cone, and must then establish conditional multiplier
quantile validity for that expansion.  Neither required link is a consequence
of the frozen premises.
